reading: Fourteen `src/app/*/[token]` route families verify against nine `token_hash` tables in `src/db/schema.ts` (waiver_records, booking_capabilities, calendar_feeds, display_tokens, person_shelf_tokens, account_tokens, two unsubscribe tables, shop_contact_email_confirmation_tokens) plus two stateless HMAC modules, `src/lib/recap-links.ts` (103 lines) and `src/lib/gift-links.ts` (110), which share a byte-identical 43-character signature guard. The 32-byte/SHA-256 primitive is written three times (`src/lib/bearer-tokens.ts`, `waiver-tokens.ts`, `account-tokens.ts`), minted by 12 `issue*`/`sign*` functions from 39 files and checked by 11 `verify*`/`check*`/`resolve*` functions across 10 modules, with 6 further "dead but ours" resolvers in two vocabularies (`kind: dead|unknown` in `src/db/seat-claims.ts` and `recap.ts`, `state: unavailable|expired` in `waivers.ts:764`). Lifecycle is spelled five ways — `expires_at` on 7 of 9 tables, `revoked_at` on 4, `used_at`+`superseded_at` on 2, nothing on the 2 unsubscribe tables — and "what does asking twice do" has five answers (waiver reuses via `token_sealed`; booking mints another capped by `MAX_LIVE_CAPABILITIES_PER_PURPOSE` 20; shelf mints another to count phones, capped at 20; calendar rotates under a unique live index; account and contact-email supersede). The two 20-link caps and their oldest-first retire (14 references, 11 lines) exist only because a stored digest cannot be read back — `src/db/booking-capabilities.ts:17-19` says "Minting is unavoidably per-request" — and ADR 20260820's `token_sealed` under `SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY` works around the same fact for one table. The 13 page routes each carry a `layout.tsx` (379 lines in all, pairwise different by one docblock line and a function name), an `error.tsx` (292 lines) and a `loading.tsx`, and 13 `unavailable*` copy pairs per locale (26 keys in en-US `diver.json`, 26 in es-ES) say "this link isn't available" thirteen ways. The genuinely one-shaped parts are `ExpiredLinkCard` with `EntryShell`'s two-tier dead-link law, `redactCapabilityUrl`'s list asserted against the filesystem (`src/app/observability.test.ts`), `src/app/capability-refusals.test.ts`, and the 220-line `scripts/check-capability-runbook.mjs` that keeps the 508-line runbook's 20-row table complete. ADR 20260827-the-divers-thread decision 4 folded `/recap` into `/ready`'s after-state and kept `src/app/recap/[token]/page.tsx` (278 lines), `recap-links.ts` and the mint at `src/db/recap.ts:1357` "so existing recap links keep working" — under H-49 there are none. Of the 14 families, six (`ready`, `waivers`, `recap`, `shelf`, `claim`, `gift`) already share `ThreadShell` and are one diver's relationship with one shop; the other eight are five other audiences — an account holder (3), a shop's mailbox (1), a staffer's calendar client (1), a lobby device (2) and an opt-out (1).

ideas.title: Nine token tables are one capabilities table
ideas.reading: Nine tables in `src/db/schema.ts` carry `token_hash` (lines 3452, 3481, 3510, 5735, 6034, 6432, 6482, 6566, 9292), each with its own issue/verify/revoke module: `src/db/booking-capabilities.ts` (456 lines), `display-tokens.ts` (297), `person-shelf-tokens.ts` (265), `account-tokens.ts` (163), `shop-contact-email.ts`, `courtesy-email.ts`, `last-minute-list.ts`, `waiver-issue.ts` (548) and `src/features/calendar-sync/feed-store.ts`. ADR 20260804-seat-claim-links rejected "a new claim-token table" because it "duplicates booking_capabilities' hashing, expiry, revocation, and cap machinery for no isolation gain", and the four tables added after it (display_tokens, person_shelf_tokens, shop_contact_email_confirmation_tokens, and the shelf's twin of the 20-cap) each did exactly that. The only axis that differs is the subject — a booking, a person at a shop, a waiver record, a user account, a shop, a staffer's scope, a last-minute entry — and `trip_invitations_source_reference_check` (schema.ts:3385-3391) already shows one table holding typed nullable subjects under a check constraint. Lifecycle is spelled five ways across the nine (expires_at 7, revoked_at 4, used_at+superseded_at 2, none 2), retention covers 3 of 9 (`src/lib/retention.ts:205-234`; `booking_capabilities` has no window, #1726), and `src/db/anonymize.ts` sweeps them at 8 separate sites (lines 702, 843, 848, 920, 936, 945, 965, 1072). The runbook's 20-row table (`docs/engineering/capability-telemetry-runbook.md:69-88`) restates each family's lifetime and revocation in prose, and the 220-line guard checks only that each purpose is mentioned somewhere. Eight `src/app/api/test/seed-*` routes exist to seed one token kind each.
ideas.idea: One `capabilities` table: `purpose` (one enum of every kind now spread over four enums and five single-purpose tables), `shop_id`, typed nullable subject columns (`booking_id`, `person_id`, `waiver_record_id`, `user_account_id`, `list_entry_id`) under a per-purpose check constraint, `expires_at`, `revoked_at`, `revoked_reason` (`used | superseded | revoked | erased`), `issued_at`, `last_used_at`. One policy record per purpose in `src/lib/capabilities.ts` — lifetime rule, single-use or not, supersede-on-issue or not, the dead page's disclosure tier, and the audience — so the runbook's table is generated from it and the guard compares rows to policy instead of hunting for mentions. One `issueCapability`, one `verifyCapability({ purpose })` whose predicate carries the purpose (the `verifyDisplayToken` discipline, for every kind), one `revokeCapabilities({ subject, purpose? })`, one retention row (`capabilities: 90` past expiry), one erasure sweep by subject. Purpose-specific facts stay on the thing the capability opens and point at it — a `display_screens` row keeps `label`, `show_names`, `last_shown_at`; `calendar_feeds` keeps `scope` — and the credential columns leave those rows. The two stateless bearer shapes fold in as purposes too: `gift` and the forwardable postcard become read-only rows that `claimSeatRecord`'s revoke-all does not touch, which is what `gift-links.ts` exists to guarantee by another route — leaving `?gate=` and `?preview=`, signed sentences rather than credentials, as the only HMACs. One `seed-capability` test route replaces eight.
ideas.dissolves: Eight of nine token tables, ten issue/verify/revoke modules, three copies of the primitive, `recap-links.ts` and `gift-links.ts` with `RECAP_LINK_SECRET`/`GIFT_LINK_SECRET`, seven of eight seed routes, and the hand-written half of the runbook.
ideas.scope: src/db/schema.ts (9 tables → 1 plus subject rows), src/db/booking-capabilities.ts, display-tokens.ts, person-shelf-tokens.ts, account-tokens.ts, shop-contact-email.ts, courtesy-email.ts, last-minute-list.ts, waiver-issue.ts, src/features/calendar-sync/feed-store.ts, src/lib/capabilities.ts (new), src/lib/bearer-tokens.ts, waiver-tokens.ts, account-tokens.ts, recap-links.ts, gift-links.ts, src/lib/retention.ts, src/db/retention.ts, src/db/anonymize.ts, the four schema coverage guards (export/diver-merge/delete-path/retention tests), the 14 route families' verify calls, config/env-registry.mjs, docs/engineering/capability-telemetry-runbook.md, scripts/check-capability-runbook.mjs, 8 src/app/api/test/seed-* routes and the e2e specs that call them, glossary 'capability', one ADR superseding 20260723 and amending 20260804/20260730/20260725
ideas.firstSlice: Add `capabilities` and `src/lib/capabilities.ts` with the policy table, then move `display_tokens` and `person_shelf_tokens` (the two newest, one purpose each) onto it, deleting both tables, both db modules and their two seed routes, so `/board`, `/check-in` and `/shelf` verify through the one path.
ideas.conflicts: ADR 20260723-booking-capabilities (extended: its 'one table, purpose-bound' becomes the rule for every kind); ADR 20260804-seat-claim-links (its no-new-table argument applied to the four tables added after it); ADR 20260730-calendar-feed-subscriptions and 20260820-waiver-links-are-reused-not-reissued (their lifetimes become policy rows, behaviour unchanged); ADR 20260725-account-lifecycle-emails (account_tokens folded); #1726 (subsumed by one retention row); #1778 and #1774 (a staff 'links' panel and its trail event become one generic revoke); H-49 (the migration is drop-and-create, no backfill)

ideas.title: A capability's token is derived from its row, never stored
ideas.reading: Every stored kind keeps a SHA-256 digest and nothing readable (`src/lib/bearer-tokens.ts:47-51`), so no render, email or "Copy link" can hand back a link that already exists — `src/db/booking-capabilities.ts:17-19` says "Minting is unavoidably per-request… a page render that needs a link has no choice but to issue one". Four mechanisms exist only to live with that fact: `MAX_LIVE_CAPABILITIES_PER_PURPOSE` and `MAX_LIVE_SHELF_TOKENS` (20 each, 14 references, 11 oldest-first lines), `waiver_records.token_sealed` under `SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (ADR 20260820, schema.ts:6036-6061), the confirm→readiness exchange route (`src/app/s/[shopSlug]/trips/[id]/ready/route.ts`, added because a reload minted rows past the cap), and the two rescues (`src/db/readiness-link-rescue.ts`, 223 lines, and `emailFreshWaiverLink`) with their `current_link_live` guards. "What does asking twice do" therefore has five answers across the nine tables (reuse, mint-another-capped, mint-another-to-count-phones, rotate, supersede), and 39 files contain a mint call. ADR 20260820 considered deriving the token from the record id — "genuinely attractive… rejected on ordering, not on merit: the token must exist before the row it is derived from does… Worth revisiting if a second surface ever needs the same trick" — and the shelf (`src/db/person-shelf-tokens.ts:60-68`, one row per send) is that second surface. The ordering objection assumes a `token_hash not null unique` column; with no hash column the id is generated before insert and there is nothing left to order. `bearer-tokens.ts:53-58` rejects a keyed digest because rotation "would make every stored row unreadable", which a `key_version` column answers the way `recap-links.ts` and `gift-links.ts` already accept a dedicated secret.
ideas.idea: A capability's URL segment is `id.HMAC(key_v, id)`: the row's uuid plus a 43-character signature under an HKDF-derived key named by the row's `key_version`; the table stores no secret at all. Verify is parse → timing-safe check → load the row by id → check purpose, expiry, revocation and subject status — today's predicate minus the hash lookup — and a dump yields ids and nothing a browser can present. Issuing becomes idempotent: one live row per (subject, purpose) under a partial unique index (the `calendar_feeds_live_person_scope_idx` shape at schema.ts:6512-6514), and every email, reminder, "Copy link" and "Send the link" recomputes the same URL from the same row. Retiring a leaked link is one act with one meaning — revoke the row, mint a new id — so supersede, rotate and cap collapse into revoke. A key rotation signs new rows under the new version while old rows verify under theirs until they expire or are revoked, so nothing goes dark at once. `token_sealed` and the waiver's `SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY` dependency go, because a reusable link no longer needs a readable copy, and `opens`/`last_used_at` on the one row answers the shelf's "how many phones" as "how often, and when".
ideas.dissolves: `token_hash` on every table, `token_sealed`, both 20-link caps and their oldest-first retire, the confirm→readiness exchange route, the two rescues' live-link guards, and four of the five answers to 'what does asking twice do'.
ideas.scope: src/lib/bearer-tokens.ts (becomes the derive/verify pair with key versions), every token_hash reader (10 modules), src/db/schema.ts (drop 9 hash columns and token_sealed, add key_version and the live partial indexes), src/db/waivers.ts and waiver-issue.ts (secret-box caller removed), config/env-registry.mjs (one link-key entry replaces RECAP/GIFT secrets and the waiver's use of SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY), src/app/s/[shopSlug]/trips/[id]/ready/route.ts (deleted), src/db/readiness-link-rescue.ts, src/lib/kiosk-check-in.ts CAPABILITY_TOKEN_SHAPE, bearer-tokens.test.ts and booking-capabilities.test.ts, the runbook's 'Rotating or revoking' section, ADRs 20260723 and 20260820 superseded in part
ideas.firstSlice: Replace `createBearerToken`/`hashBearerToken` with `capabilityToken(id, keyVersion)` / `capabilityFromToken(token)` and move `booking_capabilities` onto it, deleting `MAX_LIVE_CAPABILITIES_PER_PURPOSE` and the exchange route, so `bookSpot`, the reminders and `/shelf`'s 'open this trip' all hand out the booking's one readiness URL.
ideas.conflicts: ADR 20260820-waiver-links-are-reused-not-reissued (its alternative 3 adopted; its ordering objection shown gone; token_sealed removed); ADR 20260723-booking-capabilities (hashed-only storage and 'no supersession on reissue' replaced by one live row per subject+purpose); src/lib/bearer-tokens.ts's key-rotation argument (answered by key_version); ADR 20260820-one-page-after-booking's exchange route (deleted with its reason); H-16 (a second one-time cutover of the same shape, no dual-read under H-49); composes with L04-1 but does not require it

ideas.title: The diver holds one link, and the shelf is it
ideas.reading: One diver at one shop is handed up to seven credentials: `/shelf` (a year, `person_shelf_tokens`), `/ready` (trip+30 days, `booking_capabilities.readiness`), `/waivers` (7 days, `waiver_records`), `/recap` (180 days, stateless), `?handoff=` (10 minutes), the arrival QR (`arrival`, departure-bounded) and the embed's `confirm` — with `/claim` as a party member's door in and `/gift` as the giver's view. `src/app/shelf/[token]/actions.ts:238-244` opens a trip by minting a fresh readiness capability and redirecting to `/ready/<new token>`, and `src/app/ready/[token]/actions.ts:124-132` signs a waiver by minting a fresh waiver link and redirecting to `/waivers/<new token>` — each tap on the diver's own file mints a new credential to reach another page about the same person. ADR 20260827-the-divers-thread decision 4 made `/recap` "stop being a page of its own", yet `src/app/recap/[token]/page.tsx` (278 lines), `src/lib/recap-links.ts` (103) and the mint at `src/db/recap.ts:1357` remain "so existing recap links keep working" — under H-49 there are no existing links. ADR 20260820-waiver-links-are-reused exists because the link a shop re-sends is the waiver's, seven-day and hash-only, and `src/app/actions/shelf-door.ts:1-20` then explains why `/ready` may mint a shelf token and `/recap` may not — three link tiers over one person, each with its own reuse rule. The roadmap's "One 'your trip' link per diver" row (`docs/product/features/roadmap.md:614`) still anchors the one link at `/ready` and still lists the recap fold as open, while ADR 20260908-one-hand lever Z ("the capability link is promoted from one trip to the diver at the shop", H-71 m) moved the anchor to the person and shipped as `/shelf`, and the row was never updated. Six of the fourteen families already share `ThreadShell` (`claim`, `gift`, `ready`, `recap`, `shelf`, `waivers`); the other eight are an account holder (`verify`, `reset-password`, `invite`), a shop's mailbox (`confirm-contact`), a staffer's calendar client (`calendar`), a device (`board`, `check-in`) and an opt-out (`unsubscribe`).
ideas.idea: The diver's link is the shelf, minted once per person-at-shop at first booking or at the counter and carried by the confirmation email, every reminder, "Text waiver" and "Copy link"; a trip is a state under it — `/shelf/<token>/trips/<id>` renders what `/ready` renders, after-state included — and the waiver step is that trip's first row, so `/ready/[token]` and `/waivers/[token]` stop being credentials and become paths. `?handoff=` stays a ten-minute credential derived from the shelf on the tap, and the arrival QR stays its own departure-bounded purpose because it leaves on paper (issue #1600). The forwardable postcard keeps a weaker credential — read-only, no cancel, no file — but as a purpose on the same booking rather than a second signing scheme; recap emails carry it, and `/recap`'s route, `recap-links.ts` and `RECAP_LINK_SECRET` are deleted, closing the ADR's "existing links" clause under H-49. Genuinely different audiences keep their own doors: `claim` (a not-yet-known person becoming one, who on success receives their own shelf link), `gift` (a third party reading four facts), the three account tokens, `confirm-contact`, `calendar`, `board`/`check-in`, and `unsubscribe` (which must outlive everything and open nothing). The waiver's medical privacy tier moves from the link to the draft — a saved questionnaire is restored only within seven days of `started_at` — so the year-long link never shows a medical answer, which is the shelf's own rule (`src/db/shelf.ts:37-41`) held on the one page that collects one. "Ask your dive shop for a fresh link" becomes one sentence because there is one link to ask for, and the two rescues (`readiness-link-rescue.ts`, `emailFreshWaiverLink`) become "send my link" to the address on file.
ideas.dissolves: The readiness and waiver links as credentials, `/recap/[token]` with `recap-links.ts`, `shelf-door.ts`'s three-tier explanation, ADR 20260820's reuse mechanism, and two of the three diver-facing 'ask for a fresh link' rescues.

ideas.conflicts: roadmap 'One your trip link per diver' (cited and gone wider: its anchor moved from /ready to the person when Z shipped, and its open recap half was closed by ADR 20260827 decision 4 — the row is stale); ADR 20260827-the-divers-thread decision 4 ('existing recap links keep working' is an H-49 deletion); ADR 20260908-one-hand lever Z and H-71 (m) (the promotion it named, finished); ADR 20260820-waiver-links-are-reused-not-reissued (superseded: reuse is the one link's nature); ADR 20260723-post-trip-recap (stateless recap replaced by a read-only purpose); ADR 20260906-before-you-ask decision 3 (handoff unchanged); ADR 20260804-seat-claim-links (claim stays and hands the claimant their shelf link); ADR 20260821-the-ready-page-asks-once (its rows unchanged, re-homed); settled 'the diver's trip page and the staff trip page stay separate' (untouched)

ideas.title: Fourteen doors are one route group with one refusal
ideas.reading: Thirteen `src/app/*/[token]/layout.tsx` files (379 lines) exist "for one reason" — the error-boundary copy bridge of ADR 20260803 — and differ pairwise by one docblock line and the function name (`diff verify/[token]/layout.tsx reset-password/[token]/layout.tsx` is 2 lines); thirteen `error.tsx` (292 lines) and thirteen `loading.tsx` sit beside them. `src/app` has no route group at all, and a `(doors)` group would give all fourteen one layout and one boundary without moving a URL. Thirteen `unavailable*` copy pairs per locale (26 keys in `src/i18n/locales/en-US/diver.json`, 26 in es-ES) say "This link isn't available" thirteen ways — "This readiness link", "This waiver link", "This recap link", "This screen link", "This tablet isn't set up", "This link has run out". The dead-link law has two tiers (account: name no shop; booking: name the shop — `shipped.md:1293-1300`, `EntryShell.test.tsx`), but the "dead but ours" question is answered by six resolvers in two vocabularies: `getClaimPageState`/`getRecapPageState` (`kind: dead | unknown`), `TokenWaiverState` (`state: unavailable | expired`, `src/db/waivers.ts:764`), `staleBookingCapabilityForToken` (`{ shopId }`), `shelfTokenStanding`, `wasAccountTokenConsumed`/`wasShopContactEmailConfirmed`. `ExpiredLinkCard` (100 lines) is already one shape for the card, used by 5 pages, `EntryDone` by the rest, and 13 renders wear `glyph="expired"`. `src/app/capability-refusals.test.ts` and `observability.test.ts` already scan the filesystem for `[token]` directories, so the scan would read one group.
ideas.idea: Every door lives under `src/app/(doors)/<family>/[token]/`, with one `layout.tsx` (the copy bridge), one `error.tsx` and one `loading.tsx` shape; URLs are unchanged. Verify returns one standing — `live(context) | dead(shop | null) | unknown` — with the tier decided by the purpose's policy (L04-1) rather than by six resolvers, so a page branches on `standing.kind` and nothing else. One `DeadLink` page renders the two tiers from two copy pairs (`door.unavailable.*`, `door.unavailableWithShop.*`), the family named by an eyebrow from the same bundle the live page uses; eleven pairs are deleted from both locales. `CAPABILITY_ROUTE_PREFIXES` becomes the group's directory listing — generated at build like the env registry, or asserted as today — and the paragraph-per-prefix commentary in `capability-urls.ts` moves to the policy table. The grammar afterwards: a door is a purpose, a token and a standing; the family says only which page opens when the standing is live.
ideas.dissolves: Twelve layouts, twelve error boundaries, eleven copy pairs per locale, five of six standing resolvers, and the per-family reasoning each door re-derives about what a dead link may say.
